A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicMotion, MagicData, and MagicBench. Their complete main texts, appendices A–F, seven tables, and twenty figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative evaluations on MagicBench and DAVIS, component and dataset ablations, and qualitative experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and ablations and additionally reports MagicMotion results using a Wan1.3B backbone.

M1.justification: v2 adds a Wan1.3B backbone alternative to the existing CogVideoX-based MagicMotion model (Tables 1 and 4). The Trajectory ControlNet design, progressive training stages, and segmentation loss remain unchanged; no further procedural adaptation is described.

E1.justification: MagicData training, MagicBench and DAVIS evaluation, and the MeViS/MOSE dataset ablation are retained. Appendix camera control, video editing, and alternative-trajectory scenarios are also unchanged. The revised training sample count and added backbone do not establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The same seven external comparators participate: Motion-I2V, ImageConductor, DragAnything, LeViTor, DragNUWA, SG-I2V, and Tora. The new Wan1.3B rows represent MagicMotion variants. Existing ablation controls are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported training set from 51K to 23K examples while retaining one epoch per stage. The added Wan1.3B configuration is listed with 81-frame, 480×832 output, alongside CogVideoX's 49-frame, 480×720 configuration. These substantially revise reported experimental settings, although rerunning existing experiments and reconciling Wan's output with the retained 49-frame evaluation procedure are not explained.

E4.justification: The existing MagicData ablation receives revised FID evidence in Table 2: MagicBench scores without/with MagicData change from 99.55/93.27 to 24.24/15.17. Its question and controls remain the same. Progressive-training and segmentation-loss ablations and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: v2 replaces existing FID entries in Tables 1, 2, and 5–7 and adds Wan1.3B results on both benchmarks and all six object-count groups. For example, CogVideoX Stage1 MagicBench FID changes from 87.13 to 15.06, while FVD remains 112.69. The best external MagicBench FID comparator changes from SG-I2V to Tora. The unexplained revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and diffusion, segmentation, and combined loss equations (1–3) are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction reduces MagicData's claimed scale from 51K to 23K videos. The central claims about three trajectory-control formats, the public dataset and benchmark contributions, and superiority over previous methods are retained.

C2.justification: The explanations of progressive training and segmentation loss, interpretations of multi-object results, and appendix applicability discussions remain unchanged. No substantive explanation of the revised FID values or new backbone limitations is added.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly identifies Wan1.3B and its supported output resolution and length. Existing hardware, optimizer, inference settings, and project-access information are retained. No Wan-specific training instructions or explanation of the FID computation revisions is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Wan reference associated with the additional backbone. Related-work positioning otherwise remains unchanged. StableAnimator's updated publication information describes the same cited work and does not constitute an additional research reference.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author designation and more explicit backbone labels. Section order, appendix organization, and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged; there is no substantial narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 4–7 expand to accommodate the additional backbone, with revised row labels, grouping, and local layout adjustments. All twenty figures retain their content, including the unchanged radar chart and dataset histograms.

improvement.justification: The added Wan1.3B results provide useful evidence beyond v1's single backbone. However, extensive FID revisions are unexplained, and unchanged Figure 4 conflicts with Table 7's revised SG-I2V/Tora FID ordering. The new 23K dataset description also conflicts with Figure 19, whose height histogram contains a bin above 35K. These consistency problems prevent reliably weighing the added empirical evidence against the reporting deficiencies.
